entries.reason: the enumeration is header-only: no class, no method, nothing to build and no symbol to export, so there is nothing in any library for a dylib inventory to find. The two registry kinds that exist for exactly this answer a different question of it - a header the build reads must declare the name - and `MLMultiArray.h` declares this one. Its cases are the header's own bit patterns, read from the iPhoneOS 16.4 SDK: Double and Float64 are 0x10000|64, Float32 and Float are 0x10000|32, Float16 is 0x10000|16, Int32 is 0x20000|32 The case carries no API_AVAILABLE of its own, so it has the enumeration's: ios(11.0)
entries.effect: the enumeration answers its cases at every release, which is what an enumeration is: a name for a value the compiler reads and nothing more
entries.source: MLMultiArray.h of the iPhoneOS 16.4 SDK, the declaration and its case values; the fact that the armv7 release exports the whole vecLib BLAS and LAPACK alongside it, measured over the caches from 4.3 up, is why the port can use a library whose only Swift-facing type is this one
